input.title: Usage review: a floor that asks how busy the repo was
input.head: claude/awesome-planck-p7v2nz
input.body:
The first production review ([#2237](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/2237)) reported 54 findings. The owner asked me to check the 51 `check-never-fires` among them. Fewer than half could have fired at all, and the audit found the denominator defect they predicted plus two others. Advances #2084.

## What the 51 actually were

| class | n | evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| born inside the window | 13 | `since` from 2026-09-03 to 2026-09-21; two landed on its last day |
| structurally inert in the canon | 12 | 6 gated on `.claudinite/shared`, which this repo does not have; 2 on the adoption interview; 3 on a preferences store this repo isn't; 1 on `seedOps` |
| dead scope | 1 | `in-session-github-access` scans `^(routines\|migrations)/`; the tree has **0** such files |
| tiny scope | 9 | every `gha/*` check scans `.github/workflows/` — 5 files |
| genuinely preventive | 16 | `no-conflict-markers` over 2267 files, `warning-suppression` over 912. Zero is the check working |

`fixture-git-housekeeping` is the sharpest: the review called it never-firing while it threw 13 advisories the same day. It was one day old.

## The denominator

`runs: 2276` is **one global number, byte-identical across all 51 findings** — it counts sweeps, not opportunities. A check gated on an absent path was indistinguishable from one evaluated 2276 times and finding nothing, so the floor passed always and no rule was ever gated.

It now reads `activity`, a weighted blend of the four counters the owner named, all of which the fold already recorded:

| term | weight | unit | this window |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `userMessages` | 0.40 | 1 | 624 |
| `tokensOut` | 0.20 | 100,000 | 48.7M |
| `merges` | 0.20 | 1 | 353 |
| `itemsClosed` | 0.20 | 1 | 175 |

`per` puts each term on a common scale so the **weights are the blend's only bias**; they lean on the owner's own prompts as the most direct evidence that work happened. `tokensOut` rather than `tokensIn` because input is 15.2B against 48.7M — it measures the harness's caching, not the work.

A term the record does not carry is **dropped and the remaining weights re-normalized**, never read as zero. No term recorded is `null`.

One measure, a different bar per subject kind: checks and the check scope 120, guards 90, skills 60.

**It discriminates where `runs` did not.** Over the two windows: **453** against **53.9**, an 8.4× spread. `checks-slower`'s `previous.activity ≥ 120` now correctly refuses to compare against a window that was barely active — the first time that floor has done any work.

## Two faults beyond the denominator

- **`check-never-fires` double-claimed.** No `and` clause, so it fired for every zero-firing check including the ones `check-never-fires-with-prose-twin` claimed — while asserting "and has no prose twin". `scheduler-workflows-are-thin` appeared twice in one review under two causes. The evaluator gained `!` on a live predicate: the whole of what two rules reading one record half need in order to split the subjects. Unknown still propagates through the negation.
- **`packDeclaredAt` read the clone's depth as an adoption date.** Its own comment promised a shallow clone answers `null`; it did not — `git log --reverse -S` returns the earliest commit the checkout *reaches*, which is a real commit. The canon declared these packs long before any practical fetch depth, so the same review over the same record found different things on two checkouts. A match is now trusted only when the commit before it did not already carry the pack. This is why `adopt-claudinite` was reported as an unreached adoption skill — exactly the "never fires is not strange" case.

## What this deliberately does not fix

The blend does not settle the structurally-inert or dead-scope classes; those need a **per-subject opportunity** count (could this check have fired at all), which the owner chose to defer in favour of the simpler single rate. Filed rather than built. The dead `in-session-github-access` check is filed separately — that is a bug in the check, not in the review.

Net on the real record: 54 → 51 findings, all three removed being ones that should never have been there.

## Checks

Full suite 3867/3867. `check_the_world` 0 blocking, 35 advisory — identical to `main`. `check_the_work` 0 blocking, no findings. Both new test files were watched red first: the unknown-handling tests bite when `activity` treats absence as zero, and the shallow-clone test reproduced the real defect before the fix.

Automerge: `nothing`.

input.title: in-session-github-access scans a directory that does not exist
input.body:
`packs/claudinite-growth/skills/unattended-agents/declared-checks.json` declares `in-session-github-access` with:

```
"scanFiles": "/^(routines|migrations)\\/.*\\.mjs$/"
```

Both are **root-level** paths. This tree has no root `routines/` or `migrations/` — `git ls-files 'routines/*' 'migrations/*'` returns 0. Migration records live at `packs/<pack>/migrations/`, so the pattern selects nothing and has selected nothing since whatever layout change moved them.

The check is blocking and reads as live. It cannot fire. This is the failure `writing-check-selects` names: *a pattern left behind by a layout change matches nothing, reads as live, and fixtures spelling the same dead layout keep proving the matching.*

Found while auditing the 51 `check-never-fires` findings in the first production usage review ([#2237](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/2237)). Of those 51 this was the only one whose scope was genuinely empty, so the review's rule did its job here — it just cannot distinguish this case from a check that is silent because the repository is well behaved, which is the separate opportunity-measure gap.

## What to do

- Repoint the pattern at where these files actually live (`packs/[^/]+/migrations/`, and wherever routines now are — confirm before writing, since `routines/` may have no successor here at all).
- Add the assertion `writing-check-selects` asks for: the check's own test should fail if its scope is empty against the real tree, so the next layout change is caught rather than inherited.
- If routines genuinely have no home in this repository, say so and scope the check to migrations alone rather than leaving a dead alternation.

---

input.title: A usage rule should know whether its subject could have fired at all
input.body:
Deferred from #2244, where the owner chose the single blended activity rate as the simpler start and this as the thing to revisit with a window of evidence behind it.

## The gap

`activity` answers *was the repository busy enough to judge anything*. It does not answer *could this particular subject have fired*. Those are different questions, and the second is what the first production review got wrong. Of its 51 `check-never-fires` findings:

- **12** were structurally inert in this repo — 6 gated on `.claudinite/shared`, which the canon does not have; 2 on the adoption interview; 3 on a preferences store this repo isn't; 1 on `seedOps`. They never executed.
- **9** scan `.github/workflows/`, which is 5 files.
- **1** (`in-session-github-access`, #2245) scans a directory that does not exist.

A check that never ran and a check that ran 2276 times and found nothing are indistinguishable in the record, so all of them read as evidence.

## What would close it

A per-subject opportunity count the fold records, so a rule can read `findings / opportunities` instead of `findings / activity`. For a check that is roughly *times its `relevantWhen` passed × files its scanner selected*; for a skill, the moments its triggers had, which the fold already counts.

`runActivePackRules` currently has no record distinguishing "ran and found nothing" from "never applied" — `runRule` applies `relevantWhen` internally and simply produces no findings. So the counter has to be added where relevance is decided, and the same discipline applies as to every other counter here: **absent must read as *not recorded*, never as zero**, or an older fold makes every check look unreachable.

## Why it was not done in #2244

Two mechanisms rather than one, and the owner's call was that a single readable number is worth more than precision at this stage. Worth re-opening once there is a window of `activity`-gated reviews to judge: if findings turn out uncorrelated with the blend, or the inert classes keep dominating every review, that is the evidence this measure was needed.

The retrospective (#2240) already lists every threshold and floor as cheap to re-examine, and its "is it overused" question covers exactly this.

content.text:
You were right on both counts, and the audit found a third thing neither of us had named.

## The 51, checked

Fewer than half could have fired at all.

| class | n | why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| born inside the window | 13 | `since` 2026-09-03 → 2026-09-21; two landed on its **last day** |
| structurally inert here | 12 | 6 gated on `.claudinite/shared`, which the canon doesn't have; 2 on the adoption interview; 3 on a preferences store this repo isn't; 1 on `seedOps` |
| dead scope | 1 | `in-session-github-access` scans `^(routines\|migrations)/` — the tree has **0** such files |
| tiny scope | 9 | every `gha/*` scans `.github/workflows/` — 5 files |
| genuinely preventive | 16 | `no-conflict-markers` over 2267 files. Zero is the check working |

Sharpest case: `fixture-git-housekeeping` was reported as never-firing while it threw **13 advisories** in my sweep the same day. It was one day old.

Your adoption point generalises past skills — for a legacy-tolerance advisory, an adoption-time check and a member-conformance check, **zero is the designed outcome**. The rule was treating the success state as suspicious.

## The denominator

Your diagnosis was exact. `runs: 2276` is **one global number, byte-identical in all 51 findings**. It counts sweeps. The floor passed always, so no rule was ever gated.

All four metrics you named were already in the fold, so this needed no new instrumentation. `activity` is now a weighted blend — `userMessages` 0.40, `tokensOut` 0.20, `merges` 0.20, `itemsClosed` 0.20 — each scaled by a unit so the **weights are the only bias**, leaning on your own prompts as the most direct evidence work happened. `tokensOut` not `tokensIn`, because input is 15.2B against 48.7M: it measures the harness's caching, not the work.

It discriminates where `runs` was flat: **453 this window against 53.9 the previous one**, an 8.4× spread. `checks-slower`'s `previous.activity ≥ 120` now refuses to compare against a barely-active window — the first real work that floor has done. One measure, different bars: checks 120, guards 90, skills 60, as you asked.

## The third thing

`packDeclaredAt`'s own comment promised that a shallow clone answers `null`. **It doesn't.** `git log --reverse -S` returns the earliest commit the checkout *reaches* — a real commit. The canon declared these packs long before any practical fetch depth, so the adoption window started at the clone's horizon, and the same review over the same record found different things on two checkouts. That is *why* `adopt-claudinite` was flagged. Fixed: a match is trusted only when the commit before it didn't already carry the pack.

Also fixed: `check-never-fires` carried no `and`, so it claimed every check the twin rule claimed while asserting "and has no prose twin" — `scheduler-workflows-are-thin` appeared twice under two causes.

**What this does not fix, deliberately:** the blend doesn't settle the inert or dead-scope classes. Those need a per-subject *opportunity* count, which you chose to defer. Filed as [#2246](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/2246) rather than smuggled in.

Two process notes, both mine: I hit `git checkout --` on an unstaged edit after the guard warned me — same mistake as last session — and recovered from a scratchpad copy. And my first `activity` test asserted the invariant wrongly (equal raw values aren't equal scaled values); the code was right, the test was wrong.

**Folders touched** — `packs/claudinite-growth/`: the blend and its unknown handling in `figures.mjs`, `!predicate` in `evaluate.mjs`, the shallow-clone guard in `read-live.mjs`, and seven rules' floors in `usage-rules.json`.

Suite 3867/3867, both sweeps 0 blocking, world advisories identical to `main`. Both new test files watched red first.

> ⚠️ Still open: [#2244](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/2244) awaiting your review (automerge `nothing`). [#2245](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/2245) the dead check, [#2246](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/2246) the opportunity measure you deferred. Still from earlier: [#2238](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/2238) verification, [#2240](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/2240) retrospective, [#2239](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/2239) design-doc deletion.

message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**

   Two user messages drove this session.

   **First: "lgtm"** — under the personal pack rule `lgtm-merges`, this means merge the change at hand into `main` via the `merge-to-main` skill. It approves *that change only*, never later work. The change was PR [#2214](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/2214), the usage-review loop implementing `docs/usage-review/DESIGN.md`.

   **Second (a correction + feature):** *"check the 51 check-never-fires findings - remember that "never fires" for an adoption skill is not strange, and also - the rate of invocation (per user prompts, per conversation tokens, per PR count, per closed issues) is a crucial factor. I list several comparison numbers because it's not easy to say which is the right one. It could be that a biased average of the 4 metrics (invocations per X) could be a good start."*

   Intent: audit the 51 `check-never-fires` findings the first production review reported; recognise that silence is the designed outcome for adoption-scoped elements; and replace the rules' denominator with an invocation *rate* normalised against real activity.

   Via `AskUserQuestion`, the user then chose: **"One blended activity rate is a good, simpler start. We could say that we want skills vs. checks to have different thresholds, but having one metric is nice."**

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - Claudinite canon: packs on a shelf (`packs/`), vendored into members under `.claudinite/shared/`, member-local content under `.claudinite/local/packs/`. **The canon itself has no `.claudinite/shared/`** — this is why member-scoped checks are structurally inert here.
   - The promotion ladder (platform setting → schema → hook → check → skill → prose) and the usage-review loop reading back whether a placement held.
   - **Unknown is not zero**: a counter absent from the record reads *not recorded* (`null`), never 0; propagates through the evaluator so a comparison touching one is *not evaluated* rather than false.
   - The usage-rule grammar: `<when> := <term> ('>='|'<='|'=') <term>`, `<term> := <atom> | <atom> '/' <atom>`, `<atom> := ['previous.'] ['median('] <name> [')'] | <number>`. `and` is a second comparison, a live predicate name, or (new) a `!`-prefixed predicate name.
   - Positional-tuple fold format with a self-describing `fields` header; day rows are `{ totals: [...], skillLoads: {...}, checks: {...}, checkFindings: {...}, queue: {...}, ... }` decoded by `decodeRow`.
   - Provenance: append-only one file per element, closed kind vocabulary (`born`, `reworded`, `weakened`, `strengthened`, `policy-changed`, `severity-changed`, `retired`, …), `Mechanism` required on `born`/`policy-changed`/`severity-changed`/etc.
   - See-it-fail discipline: every new test mutated against its subject to prove it bites.
   - Action guards in this repo that fired: `merge-main-into-branch`, `checkout-restores-index`, `bare-sleep-wait`, `pipe-tail-hides-exit`, `github-api-via-shell`, `shell-write-to-skill-scoped-path`, `check-sweep-read-blocking-only`, `ask-user-question-already-decided`, `issue-labels-overwrite`, `sub-issue-without-parent`, `github-list-without-fields`, `skill-not-loaded-for-call`.

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   **`packs/claudinite-growth/tasks/usage-review/figures.mjs`** — the one place the review's vocabulary meets the record's. Added the blended denominator:
   ```js
   export const ACTIVITY_TERMS = Object.freeze({
     userMessages: Object.freeze({ weight: 0.4, per: 1 }),
     tokensOut: Object.freeze({ weight: 0.2, per: 100_000 }),
     merges: Object.freeze({ weight: 0.2, per: 1 }),
     itemsClosed: Object.freeze({ weight: 0.2, per: 1 }),
   });

   export function activityOf(readTerm) {
     let weighted = 0;
     let covered = 0;
     for (const [name, { weight, per }] of Object.entries(ACTIVITY_TERMS)) {
       const value = readTerm(name);
       if (value === null || value === undefined || !Number.isFinite(value)) continue;
       weighted += weight * (value / per);
       covered += weight;
     }
     return covered === 0 ? null : weighted / covered;
   }
   ```
   And in `FIGURES`:
   ```js
   activity: (subject, w) => activityOf((name) => (name === 'itemsClosed'
     ? sumEveryKey(w.days, 'queue', 'done')
     : sumScalar(w.days, name))),
   ```
   `tokensOut` rather than `tokensIn` because input is 15.2B against 48.7M — it measures the harness's caching, not the work. A term not recorded is dropped and remaining weights re-normalized, never read as zero.

   **`packs/claudinite-growth/tasks/usage-review/evaluate.mjs`** — added `!` negation on a live predicate so two rules reading one record half split the subjects:
   ```js
   if (rule.and) {
     const negated = !andComparison && rule.and.startsWith('!');
     const raw = andComparison
       ? holds(andComparison, read)
       : predicateOf(subject, negated ? rule.and.slice(1) : rule.and);
     // Unknown survives the negation: a predicate that could not be read is
     // still unread when the rule asked for its absence.
     const also = negated && raw !== null ? !raw : raw;
   ```
   `ruleSentence` renders `!proseTwin` as `not proseTwin`.

   **`packs/claudinite-growth/tasks/usage-review/read-live.mjs`** — `packDeclaredAt` rewritten; its old comment promised a shallow-clone guard that did not exist:
   ```js

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.

- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- backfilling-provenance: Filling a pack's empty provenance files from its history - each entry derived from the adding commit, its pull request and the version log before the rule is re-read, every commit that touched the pack weighed whether or not a draft covers it, and the README and manifest trimmed to use in the same change. Use when a pack under packs/ or .claudinite/local/packs/ carries empty provenance files, or when asked to backfill or write a pack's provenance.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- changing-pack-elements: What a change to a pack's element owes - the entry on its provenance file, which kind, and how to append it - and what a pack's README carries. Loaded for any edit of a pack's RULES.md, skills, checks, tasks, manifest, README or provenance folder, in a repo's local pack or on a canon's shelf.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- committing: How a commit is cut — one concern per commit, the issue it references, a landed commit revised only by a new one, files staged by name. Use before any git commit.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.

However, if they ask for a document, page, report, memo, or notes WITHOUT naming a file format and the session offers Claude's own dedicated document or page skill or connector, use that instead. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
