The owner declined a skill predicting its own usage. `loads-per-sessions: 1 in 20`
on bug-investigation was a number I invented; the one rule that read it,
`skill-routine-under-rate`, divided observed loads by that guess and reported the
result as evidence about the skill. It is retired with the key.

That forces the vocabulary. Without a rate, `routine` and `rare` both mean "zero
says nothing, never a finding" - two spellings of one state, which the
declared-field rule forbids. Both become `judgment`, and the three survivors each
name a MECHANISM the record can contradict: loaded while its pack is adopted,
loaded by its own force-load declarations, or loaded when the model judges its
description fits. A guess cannot be wrong in a way a counter detects.

The same change answers the second finding. `ci-performance-evaluation` was
`rare`, which is false - a weekly task reaches for it. I had applied `rare` as a
bulk default to 17 skills without judging them one at a time, and it was caught on
the first one opened. Under the new set it claims `judgment`, which is true of it
and of every other trigger-less skill, checked one by one.

The check gains the half of an expectation a file can settle: `triggered` while
declaring no force-load trigger has no moments to be judged against. The converse
stays legal - a skill may carry a trigger and still expect most loads by judgment,
which is a real claim about itself - and a retired key in the block is now refused
rather than ignored, since a key nothing reads is a claim the record never tests.

Three faults the first production review exposed, and the denominator the
owner asked for.

The floor read `runs` or `sessions`. `runs` is one global number the window
carries once - 2276, identical in every one of the 54 findings - so the
floor passed always and no rule was ever gated. It now reads `activity`: a
weighted blend of what the owner asked for, what the conversation cost,
what shipped and what closed, each scaled to a common unit so the weights
are the blend's only bias. One measure, a different bar per subject kind.
Over the two windows it was calibrated on the blend moves 8.4x (453 against
54) where `runs` was flat, so `checks-slower` now refuses to compare against
a window that was barely active.

`check-never-fires` carried no `and`, so it also claimed every check the
prose-twin rule claimed, while its text said "and has no prose twin". The
review reported one check twice under two causes. The evaluator gained `!`
on a live predicate - the whole of what two rules reading one record half
need to split the subjects between them.

`packDeclaredAt` promised in its own comment that a shallow clone answers
null. It did not: `git log --reverse -S` returns the earliest commit the
checkout REACHES, so the adoption window started at the clone's horizon and
one review over one record found different things on two checkouts. The
match is now trusted only when the commit before it did not already carry
the pack.

# Running the suite

- **The whole suite is one command** — `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`. There is no test
  script; `ci.yml`'s array is not authoritative. A bash glob without `globstar` is the dangerous
  substitute — `packs/*/test/*.test.mjs` reports nothing wrong over 125 of 314 files — while
  `node --test <dir>` fails outright and a glob matching nothing exits 1, so only a glob that
  matches a subset leaves you believing a green run. (whole-suite-command)
- **Read a run's output from a file** — redirect one run and grep that file for the slice you need;
  never re-run the ~55s suite to re-slice unchanged output. (read-runs-output)
- **`git add` a new test file before certifying a run green** — `git ls-files` excludes an unstaged
  file, so the run never executed it; the `untracked-test-file` finding at Stop says which.
  (git-add-new)
- **Iterating on a sweep across many files** — run only the test files the edit touches, plus
  `check_the_work`; spend the whole suite and `check_the_world` once, at the end. Both are
  whole-tree aggregates whose verdict cannot turn on one file. (iterating-sweep-across)
- **Editing a `RULES.md` or `README.md` under `packs/`** — the file that holds a pack's rule index
  in step with its prose sits outside the pack, and neither conformance sweep runs it, so add
  `node --test engine-tests/rule-index.test.mjs` to the files the edit touches. (editing-rules-md)
